topic: Psychological and Social Principles of Physical Education
subject: pe

items.title: Lactate is not metabolic waste
items.claim: For decades lactic acid was described as the cause of muscle fatigue and post-exercise soreness. What does current physiology say?

options.text: Lactate directly causes delayed onset muscle soreness
Lactate is an important metabolic fuel, recycled to glucose and used by tissues
It has no role in metabolism
It is only present at rest

items.reveal_title: Lactate is a fuel, not a waste product
items.reveal:
Brooks's lactate shuttle hypothesis (1986, refined since) describes lactate produced in one tissue being transported to and oxidised by others, or recycled to glucose in the liver (Cori cycle).

Delayed onset muscle soreness is now attributed to micro-damage and inflammation, not lactate.
items.why: Sport-science textbooks lagged decades behind physiological evidence in changing this terminology.

items.title: BMI's limits for athletes
items.claim: Body Mass Index (Quetelet, 1830s; popularised in the 20th century) is a single number from mass over height squared. Why is it problematic for athletes?

options.text: It does not distinguish lean mass from fat mass, so muscular athletes are often classified overweight or obese
It is unrelated to body shape

items.reveal:
Rugby forwards, weightlifters and bodybuilders routinely fall above the 'overweight' or 'obese' threshold despite low body fat.

DXA, hydrostatic weighing and skinfolds give better composition data for performance contexts.
items.why: Population-level measures and individual measures answer different questions.

items.title: The 10,000-hour rule
items.claim: Anders Ericsson's research on expertise was popularised as a '10,000-hour rule' by Malcolm Gladwell. What did Ericsson himself say about it?

options.text: He coined and endorsed the simple rule
He argued deliberate practice mattered, but rejected the simple hours-to-mastery shorthand
He said hours did not matter at all
He demonstrated 100 hours is sufficient for any sport

items.reveal_title: Ericsson pushed back on the round number
items.reveal:
Ericsson's Peak (2016) and earlier papers emphasised deliberate, structured practice with feedback, and noted that hours alone are insufficient. He criticised the 10,000-hour shorthand.

Macnamara et al. (2014) meta-analysis found practice accounted for variable proportions of expertise depending on domain.
items.why: Popular versions of research findings can outlive the researcher's own corrections.
